stops.note: 'to be able'; the same infinitive, through Medieval Latin posse comitatus 'the force of the county', later gave English 'posse'

Vulgar Latin reshaped posse as *potere; the Oaths of Strasbourg of 842, the oldest text in early French, promise loyalty 'in quant Deus savir et podir me dunat' (as far as God gives me knowledge and power)
the 'balance of power' became a stated principle of European diplomacy in the Treaty of Utrecht of 1713

current_meaning: the ability or authority to do something; energy supplied for use
